what_its_for: Oxazepam is used to relieve anxiety and nervousness. It can also help with anxiety related to depression and is used to help manage alcohol withdrawal symptoms, such as shaking, sweating, and agitation.
how_to_take: Take oxazepam by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it exactly as your doctor prescribed — do not take more than directed or take it more often than prescribed. This medicine can become habit-forming, so only use it for as long as your doctor tells you to.
dosing: Your doctor will set the right dose for you based on your condition, age, and other health factors. For anxiety, typical doses range from 10 mg to 30 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day. For alcohol withdrawal, doses may be higher under close medical supervision. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store oxazepam at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about a local take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking oxazepam — it can cause dangerous drowsiness and slow your breathing. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Do not take other sedatives, sleeping pills, opioid pain medicines, or muscle relaxers without your doctor's approval. Do not stop taking oxazepam suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause serious withdrawal symptoms including seizures.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: trouble breathing or very slow breathing, severe drowsiness or confusion, thoughts of harming yourself or suicide, unusual mood or behavior changes, memory problems, signs of an allergic reaction (rash, swelling, trouble breathing), or signs of dependence or misuse. Also call your doctor if your anxiety does not improve or gets worse.
when_it_works: Oxazepam typically begins to work within 1 to 2 hours after taking a dose, so you may feel calmer or more relaxed fairly quickly. However, it works best when taken consistently as prescribed. Tell your doctor if you do not notice any improvement after a few days.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with extra caution — older adults are more sensitive to this medicine and are at higher risk for falls, confusion, and excessive drowsiness. Lower doses are usually recommended. Pregnancy: Do not take oxazepam if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can harm the unborn baby and cause withdrawal symptoms in newborns. Breastfeeding: Oxazepam passes into breast milk and may harm a nursing baby — talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Safety and dosing in children have not been well established; use is not generally recommended in children under 6 years old.
